correctness.rationale: In the repair, harmonicity forces the flux c_j[1+χ(j+1)−χ(j)] to be constant, which must equal n/R, and the invariant residue measure is uniform. The spectral gap at zero gives an analytic scaled cumulant generating function for unwrapped displacement at any fixed start. The two winding terms put nk in the cosh. The rooted tree coefficient is nCR with C=product of conductances, and the ratio of quadratic to linear coefficients of P(z) is the inverse-eigenvalue sum T. Fourth-order expansion therefore gives κ4/κ2=n²−12nT/R=n²−12K/R, with K the sum of two-point effective resistances. For each oriented distance d the arc resistance is (R/n)[d+χ(i+d)−χ(i)]; translating i cancels the linear term, and summing the squared differences over ordered pairs gives 2n² Varπ(χ). The homogeneous term is R(n²−1)/12. Hence K has exact deficit R Varπ(χ), and κ4/κ2−1=12 Varπ(χ). The vanishing case is exactly constant χ, equivalently uniform rates. I independently checked the frozen winding and forest coefficients by exact determinant interpolation and its energy algebra, then ran the newly written repaired verifier: 48 exact full-generator cumulant, harmonic-coordinate, and effective-resistance comparisons passed.
residual_risks: Assumes finite positive symmetric bonds, integer period n≥3, unit lattice steps and unwrapped displacement. Finite tests do not replace the analytic proof or assert anything about finite-time kurtosis.

evidence: At equilibrium, Eq. (53) bounds λ(z) between 2Dn²[cosh(z/n)−1] and 2D[cosh(z)−1], with equal second-order coefficients. The implied winding ratio is between 1/n² and 1. Appendix C gives the inverse-polynomial winding formula for general unicyclic networks.

Ptaszyński explicitly treats higher normalized winding cumulants in more general unicyclic cases, deriving bounds for special unidirectional families and testing bidirectional extensions numerically. Wachtel–Vollmer–Altaner compute general cumulants implicitly from the tilted characteristic polynomial. None of these inspected formulas states the all-profile corrector-variance deficit.

value.rationale: At fixed total resistance the diffusivity is already known and identical for all profiles. The precise excess at fourth order answers what the envelope cannot: how strongly an arbitrary profile differs from homogeneous transport, using only its spatial corrector variance and no tilted eigenvalue computation. The equality exposes the quadratic dependence and spatial accumulation of resistance fluctuations for any contrast; this is the structurally useful contribution, independently of the already known bounds or the two-barrier example.
residual_risks: One-dimensional symmetric bond model only; no broader homogenization theorem or fixed-inventory optimization is now claimed.
